rows.consequence: The code maintains two overlapping transport APIs and, for remote runs, two SSH transport instances without delivering the documented interchangeable composition. Local command/copy implementation and its tests preserve surface that the canonical run path does not consume.
rows.counterevidence: Connection metadata is genuinely consumed; the generic methods are directly tested; NodeWorkerClient needs richer run/put/collect operations; future transfer work may need a transport boundary.
evidence_refs: boundary trace joulewise/controller.py:377-410: resolve_transport result is stored, then only connection_metadata is called
bounded absence search: git grep for run_command( and collect_artifact( outside tests found definitions only; tests contain the callers
bounded construction search: production NodeWorkerClient/SshTransport construction occurs at joulewise/adapters/__init__.py:104-105, separately from resolve_transport's SSH construction at line 203
rows.finding: The generic TransportAdapter execution/copy abstraction has no production execution role. The controller resolves it and calls only connection_metadata, while remote runtime and telemetry resolution separately constructs another SshTransport plus NodeWorkerClient. LocalTransport.run_command/collect_artifact and the equivalent generic SSH wrappers have only test callers.

rows.consequence: Cross-runtime suite semantics occupy hundreds of parallel lines and can drift even though the contract requires identical marker and status policy across runtimes.
rows.counterevidence: Generation and prompt materialization are backend-specific, and keeping the mock partially independent has oracle value; simplification should retain independent backend behavior rather than sharing the generation implementation.
rows.finding: MockRuntimeAdapter and MlxRuntimeAdapter independently implement the same suite-order traversal, block/level/item framing, status aggregation, output assembly, suite provenance, suite identity, and prompt-closure policy.

rows.consequence: Cleanup, evidence preservation, and clock metadata are integrity-sensitive seams; parallel implementations increase maintenance cost and permit runtime/telemetry behavior to diverge unintentionally.
rows.counterevidence: Runtime and telemetry operations have different artifacts, failure semantics, timeouts, and detached-process maps; node_worker.py must remain self-contained and cannot import controller-side helpers.
rows.finding: Remote lifecycle plumbing is duplicated both between VllmRuntimeAdapter and NvidiaSmiTelemetryAdapter and inside node_worker.py: worker-log preservation, result metadata, clock-alignment capture, run-id selection, process-object shutdown, and PID termination each have parallel implementations.

rows.consequence: A future or noncanonical caller can make an absolute run_id escape remote_work_root or use traversal components in either identifier, turning cleanup into deletion outside the task's isolated run directory.
rows.counterevidence: The canonical controller passes RunBundleWriter.run_id, which is sanitized to [a-z0-9_-], and current adapters generate fixed-format task IDs. The present canonical run path is therefore protected upstream.
evidence_refs: bounded absence search: grepped sanitize|normpath|isabs|basename across node_client.py, node_worker.py, and node_worker_protocol.md; no identifier-path validation found
behavior trace: posixpath.join('/tmp/joulewise','/var/tmp') produced '/var/tmp'; traversal task IDs remained in generated artifact paths
counterevidence boundary trace joulewise/bundle.py:58-90: canonical generated/config run IDs are sanitized before RunContext construction
rows.finding: The node-client boundary accepts any nonempty run_id and task_id, embeds them directly into remote paths, and later passes the derived paths to rm -rf. Neither the client, worker validation, nor protocol contract constrains them to safe path components.
